executable_probe: 1. On a throwaway document, create the element: browser_create_tab {tab_type: 'Variable Studio', confirm_mutation: true} (T6).

2. Activate it (browser_activate_tab) and, through the UI, add ONE row whose NAME is the sentinel `mcpProbeAlpha` with value `3 mm`. The sentinel is what makes the probe findable without knowing any selector in advance.

3. Run browser_eval with the expression below. It walks the DOM for the sentinel text and returns its ancestor chain (tag/id/class/role/aria-label/data-*), the sibling cells next to it, and every input/button in the nearest table-ish container — i.e. the name cell, the value cell, the row element and the add-row control, all discovered rather than guessed.

4. Record the answer as a new section of onshape_docs/experience/browser-automation.md with the same measured-live discipline as section 8 (labels, row structure, measurement date), then delete the throwaway element (browser_delete_element).
5. ONLY THEN design the browser-leg read/write. Until this is recorded the browser leg must keep refusing; the REST leg (T9) already covers the capability.

checks.pass_criteria: With a Feature Studio tab active while a second, no-longer-active `.ace_editor` node is still in the DOM, annotationCount/errors describe the VISIBLE buffer: a deliberate error in the visible source is reported, and a clean visible source does not inherit the stale node's annotations (state `editorCount`/`visibleEditors` from the same call). With no visible editor at all (a Part Studio tab active), the call answers found:false with the resolution reason instead of the other node's annotations. Deploy acceptance reads these same fields, so this check guards `compiled` itself.
checks.if_it_fails: the visibility rule (isConnected + non-zero bounding rect) does not separate the two nodes in the real DOM; re-derive it from that measurement before trusting any compile verdict.
